text:
Alex: Novus sent an RFP for an on-prem 'EdgeProof' pilot. They want a 6-week POC, HSM support, per-tenant isolation, and a capability table mapping to their checklist. Attached security questionnaire. They asked: KMS/HSM flow, FedRAMP-like controls, latency target <100ms p50 for chat, data residency (no egress), and pricing for small dedicated pool vs on-prem license. Can we sync?

Marta: Got it. Can you drop the questionnaire here? Also need to know which model family they're testing (gpt-style chat or smaller embed models).

Alex: Uploading questionnaire now: https://internal.redwood/docs/novus/edgeproof-sq.pdf They said 'redwood-verified' 13B for embeddings and 70B for chat.

Chris: 70B on-prem is heavy. Two realistic options: (1) deploy 8x A100-class nodes with quantized weights (q4o/q4f) — recommended to hit cost/latency, or (2) suggest a 13B distilled chat variant to meet <100ms p50. Also for <100ms we need NVMe-backed KV cache and tuned batching. I can provide perf numbers.

Priya: Ops note: on-prem installs require out-of-band license checks and optional telemetry egress. Customer must whitelist our install IPs and provide bastion/SSO creds for initial setup. Hardware procurement + scheduling makes 6 weeks tight if they need new machines.

Ben: Pricing: we can do a pilot credit — one-month Dedicated reserved at 50% off for up to 4 GPUs + 40 engineering hours. On-prem appliance = fixed license + annual support. I'll draft ranges (pilot vs full license).

Marta: For the capability mapping I can prepare a one-page matrix mapping their checklist -> Redwood deliverable: KMS via customer HSM, audit logs, model pinning, SLA fallbacks, quantized model support, sample latency baselines. Want me to include KV cache and batch recommendations?

Alex: Yes. Also they require zero data egress. Confirm whether we can keep logs and telemetry entirely in-customer VPC.

Priya: We can run with zero egress for customer data. Logs/traces can be local-only; health telemetry can be anonymized and opt-in. We'll need the signed runbook to accept reduced telemetry.

sec-bot: Security questionnaire received and scanned. Top missing items flagged: HSM integration steps, SOC2 attestation proof, encryption-at-rest architecture diagram. See ticket: /t/SQ-4123

Marta: I'll attach our SOC2 summary and an architecture diagram. Chris — can you provide HSM integration notes/snippet?

Chris: HSM integration snippet (PKCS#11 style) — minimal config we can paste to the questionnaire:

```
hsm:
  provider: 'pkcs11'
  pkcs11_slot: 2
  key_label: 'customer-signing-key'
  use_tls: true
```

We also support KMIP.

Ben: Alex — need procurement timeline + decision committee names so I can tailor contract terms. Also recommend pilot acceptance criteria: perf test (p50/p99), security checklist pass, and data residency verification.

Alex: Decision committee meets next Thursday, procurement kicks off this week. I'll share the meeting invite. Marta/Chris/Priya — please send artifacts by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Marta: :thumbsup: I'll draft the capability matrix and attach perf baselines.

Priya: I'll draft the staging runbook, list of required firewall rules, and the reduced-telemetry agreement language.

Chris: :thumbsup: I'll prepare quantized perf numbers, memory footprint chart, and a recommended deployment config for 70B vs 13B.

Ben: I'll prepare the preliminary quote + 30-day pilot contract template and a spec for required AWS/GCP instance classes if they choose cloud Dedicated instead of on-prem.

Alex: Great — DM me if you hit blockers. cc @legal for a quick look at pilot contract.

(Attached: novus_edgeproof_sq.pdf, internal link to SOC2 summary, perf-baseline-13B-70B.xlsx — will attach in follow ups)
